name: 1015 Folsom
summary: Bar on Folsom Street, San Francisco.
facts: The building was a gay bathhouse until a city order closed it in 1984.
Ira Sandler opened it as Das Klub in 1986; it became 1015 Folsom in 1989.
Its weeklies Spundae and Release featured electronic music from the 1990s.
Address: 1015 Folsom Street, San Francisco

name: Amélie
summary: Bar on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Started on Polk Street in 2006 as the original Amélie wine bar.
Serves wine flights, cocktails and small plates with live music and DJs.
Has since opened locations in New York and Washington, D.C.
Address: 1754 Polk Street, San Francisco

name: Amoeba Music
summary: Record store on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: The San Francisco store opened on November 15, 1997.
Occupies the former Park Bowl bowling alley near Golden Gate Park.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 1855 Haight Street, San Francisco

name: Bar Part Time
summary: Bar on 14th Street, San Francisco.
facts: A natural wine bar and nightclub run by founders Justin Dolezal, Jeremy Castillo and Dan Small.
Opened in September 2021 with a party featuring LCD Soundsystem's James Murphy.
The dance floor has a Danley soundsystem.
Address: 496 14th Street, San Francisco

name: Binu Bonu
summary: Bar on West Portal Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Italian wine bar from Massimiliano Conti and Lorella Degan, former owners of La Ciccia.
The name means good wine in Sardo, the language of Sardinia.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 230 West Portal Avenue, San Francisco

name: Bird and Beckett
summary: Bookstore on Chenery Street, San Francisco.
facts: Moved to Chenery Street in September 2008 after nine years on Diamond Street.
Its Cultural Legacy Project is a nonprofit presenting concerts and literary events.
Address: 653 Chenery Street, San Francisco

name: Blackbird
summary: Pub on Market Street, San Francisco.
facts: Reopened in July 2009 under owners Doug Murphy and Shawn Vergara after a four-month renovation.
The space was previously The Expansion for many years.
Address: 2124 Market Street, San Francisco

name: Bourbon and Branch
summary: Bar on Jones Street, San Francisco.
facts: Operated as a speakeasy during Prohibition from 1921 to 1933.
A bar has operated at the Jones Street site since 1867.
Reservations required
Address: 501 Jones Street, San Francisco

name: Browser Books
summary: Bookstore on Fillmore Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has served the neighborhood since 1976.
Green Apple Books bought it in 2019 and kept the Browser name.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 2195 Fillmore Street, San Francisco

name: Buddy
summary: Bar on 22nd Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened by Alvaro Rojas, Nicolas Torres, Nora Furst and Claire Sprouse.
Focuses on low-ABV cocktails, natural wine and coffee, in the former Californios space.
Address: 3115 22nd Street, San Francisco

name: Buena Vista
summary: Pub on Hyde St, San Francisco.
facts: Credited with introducing Irish coffee to the United States in 1952.
Travel writer Stanton Delaplane and owner Jack Koeppler worked out the recipe together.
Founded in 1916
Address: 2765 Hyde St, San Francisco

name: Buzzworks
summary: Bar on 11th Street, San Francisco.
facts: A SoMa sports bar and microbrewery between Slim's and DNA Lounge.
Has 40 rotating taps and 30 screens.
Address: 365 11th Street, San Francisco

name: Cafe du Nord
summary: Pub on Market Street, San Francisco.
facts: Occupies the basement of the Swedish American Hall, completed in 1907 and designed by August Nordin.
Operated as a rock club from 1991 through 2014.
Reopened in 2015 as a cocktail bar, with live shows returning two years later.
Founded in 2017
Address: 2170 Market Street, San Francisco

name: Casements
summary: Bar on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened by industry veterans Gillian Fitzgerald, Sean O'Donovan and Chris Hastings.
Irish bar with a large outdoor patio, live music and a large whiskey collection.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 2351 Mission Street, San Francisco

name: Comstock Saloon
summary: Bar on Columbus Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Restored in 2010 in a building from the Barbary Coast era.
Has an 18-foot mahogany bar top dating to the late 1890s.
Founded in 1907
Named after Henry Comstock
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 155 Columbus Avenue, San Francisco

name: delarosa
summary: Bar on Chestnut Street, San Francisco.
facts: First opened in 2010 on Chestnut Street.
Serves thin-crust Roman pizza, fresh pasta and craft cocktails.
Created by Ruggero Gadaldi, Adriano Paganini and Deborah Blum, the trio behind Beretta.
Address: 2175 Chestnut Street, San Francisco

name: DNA Lounge
summary: Nightclub on 11th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened on November 22, 1985.
Owner Jamie Zawinski, a former Netscape programmer, bought the club in 1999.
The building dates to 1920 and became a nightclub in 1983 as the leather bar Chaps.
Founded in 1985
Owned by Jamie Zawinski
Address: 375 11th Street, San Francisco

name: Dog Eared Books
summary: Bookstore on Valencia Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has sold new, used and remaindered books since 1992.
Specializes in Beat, off-beat, small press and local literature.
Partly wheelchair accessible
Address: 900 Valencia Street, San Francisco

name: Dogpatch Saloon
summary: Bar on 3rd Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has served the Dogpatch since 1912.
Counted among San Francisco's 100-year-old bars by InsideHook.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 2496 3rd Street, San Francisco

name: El Chato
summary: Spanish-style taberna featuring authentic pintxos and tapas and a highly-curated beverage program.
facts: A walk-in-only Spanish taberna serving wines by the glass and vermouth.
The menu has tapas, pintxos and cured meats, and guests are handed a porron.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 2301 Bryant Street, San Francisco

name: El Rio
summary: Bar on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1978 and recognized as a Legacy Business by the San Francisco Small Business Commission.
Founded by Malcolm Thornley and Robert Nett, inspired by leather motorcycles and Brazil.
Salsa Sundays, a live Latin music party, has run for over 30 years.
Partly wheelchair accessible
Address: 3158 Mission Street, San Francisco

name: Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
summary: Market in San Francisco.
facts: A weekly Saturday market began May 22, 1993 in front of the Ferry Building.
Run by CUESA, a nonprofit established in 1994.

name: Fool's Errand
summary: Bar on Divisadero Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 2018 by owner John Dampeer.
Dampeer previously ran Caskhouse in Noe Valley and Hamlet.
A cellar-like bar between Hayes and Grove streets.
Has outdoor seating
Partly wheelchair accessible
Address: 639a Divisadero Street, San Francisco

name: Gino and Carlo
summary: Pub on Green Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1942 in a 1907 Edwardian building.
Donato and Frank Rossi bought the bar in 1954, and it is still family-owned.
Address: 548 Green Street, San Francisco

name: Green Apple Books
summary: Bookstore on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1967 by Richard Savoy at Clement Street and Sixth Avenue.
Bought its neighbor Revolver Records in 1996.
Bought Browser Books on Fillmore Street in 2019.
Founded in 1967
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 506 Clement Street, San Francisco

name: Harry's Bar
summary: Bar on Fillmore Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1984.
Founded by Harry Denton.
The space was earlier the Silvertone Club, the Mardi Gras Tavern and Tommy Lynaugh's 2020.
21 and over
Address: 2020 Fillmore Street, San Francisco

name: Hi-Lo Club
summary: Bar on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened by the Koko Cocktails team after they left their original space.
The bar rail came from the original Koko's.
Booths are built from cable-car benches.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 1423 Polk Street, San Francisco

name: High Treason
summary: Bar on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened on Clement Street in early 2016.
Opened by sommeliers Michael Ireland, formerly of Meadowood and Quince, and John Vuong, of Ame and Gary Danko.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 443 Clement Street, San Francisco

name: Holy Water
summary: Bar on Cortland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Its cocktails are built from three to four ingredients.
Runs an 11th hour offering each night at 11 p.m., such as rare beer or stump-the-bartender.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 309 Cortland Avenue, San Francisco

name: Hôtel Biron
summary: "Wine Bar & Art Gallery".
facts: Wine bar and art gallery with rotating local artwork.
Pours 20 to 25 wines by the glass.
Address: 45 Rose Street, San Francisco

name: Hotel Utah Saloon
summary: Pub on 4th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Built in 1908 as a residential hotel with ground-floor storefronts.
Listed as a San Francisco Designated Landmark since November 2, 2018.
Address: 500 4th Street, San Francisco

name: House of Shields
summary: Bar on New Montgomery Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1908 and operated as a speakeasy during Prohibition.
Has never had a clock on the premises.
Address: 39 New Montgomery Street, San Francisco

name: Key Klub
summary: Wine bar with beer and food.
facts: Soft-opened in Lower Nob Hill in December 2021.
Revives the name of a 1950s nightclub that was at the same address.
Address: 850 Bush Street, San Francisco

name: Kona’s Street Market
summary: Bar on 3rd Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened by the team behind Pacific Cocktail Haven.
Drinks are inspired by street markets around the world.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 32 3rd Street, San Francisco

name: Last Rites
summary: Bar on 14th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Polynesian noir tiki bar that opened in June 2018.
The room is styled as the fuselage of a crashed plane in a jungle.
Has Wi-Fi
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 718 14th Street, San Francisco

name: Li Po Cocktail Lounge
summary: Historic cocktail bar known for its Chinese Mai Tai.
facts: Has operated at 916 Grant Avenue since 1937.
Known for a house Chinese Mai Tai made with baijiu.
Opened in 1937
Address: 916 Grant Avenue, San Francisco

name: Local Edition
summary: Bar on Market Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sits in the basement of the former Hearst Building, once home to San Francisco Examiner printing.
Décor draws on 1950s and 1960s newspapers, with vintage presses and archive clippings.
Takes reservations
Hosts live music
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 691 Market Street, San Francisco

name: Lone Star Saloon
summary: Bar on Harrison Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1989 and widely credited as the birthplace of the international bear movement.
Moved to Harrison St after the Loma Prieta earthquake damaged its Howard St site.
The first gay bar in the city to earn Legacy Business status.
Address: 1354 Harrison Street, San Francisco

name: Madrone Art Bar
summary: Bar on Divisadero Street, San Francisco.
facts: Operates as a changing site-specific installation art environment with live music.
Has been open since 2004.
Hosts live music
Address: 500 Divisadero Street, San Francisco

name: Mauna Loa Cocktails
summary: Bar on Fillmore St, San Francisco.
facts: John and Marie Martin opened the bar in 1939 as the Silk Hat.
Was renamed Mauna Loa in 1949.
Moved to its current Fillmore Street location on June 1, 1950.
Address: 3009 Fillmore St, San Francisco

name: Medicine for Nightmares
summary: Bookstore on 24th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Combines a bookstore and an art gallery.
Took over the storefront previously occupied by Alley Cat Bookstore & Gallery.
Address: 3036 24th Street, San Francisco

name: Moby Dick
summary: Bar on 18th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Received San Francisco Legacy Business status in 2016.
Reopened in May 2021 after a 14-month closure.
Address: 4049 18th Street, San Francisco

name: Moongate Lounge
summary: Cocktail bar on the second floor of Mister Jiu's.
facts: Opened above Mister Jiu's by the same team.
Its menu of six cocktails follows the Chinese agrarian calendar and rotates every two to three weeks.
Takes reservations
Address: 28 Waverly Place, San Francisco

name: Mr. Tipple's Recording Studio
summary: Bar on Fell Street, San Francisco.
facts: Owned by Jay Bordeleau, who also created the restaurant Maven.
Has a speakeasy-style back entrance on a side street.
Offers live jazz with craft cocktails.
Address: 39 Fell Street, San Francisco

name: Neck of the Woods
summary: Bar on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: A two-story venue with a downstairs bar and an upstairs performance floor.
The location has hosted live bands since 1973.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 406 Clement Street, San Francisco

name: Ocean Ale House
summary: Bar on Ocean Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Makes its pub food with as many house made and farm grown ingredients as possible.
Hosts regular live music events.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 1314 Ocean Avenue, San Francisco

name: Pagan Idol
summary: Bar on Bush Street, San Francisco.
facts: A tiki bar in the former home of Tiki Bob's Mainland Rendezvous.
Comes from the team behind Bourbon & Branch, Tradition and Rickhouse.
The front bar is built like the inside of a wooden ship.
Serves tiki bar
Takes reservations
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 375 Bush Street, San Francisco

name: Rickhouse
summary: Bar on Kearny Street, San Francisco.
facts: Built from salvaged Kentucky barrel staves and charred pre-1906 brick.
Specializes in whiskeys from around the world, with live music on weekends.
Address: 246 Kearny Street, San Francisco

name: Rickshaw Stop
summary: Nightclub on Fell Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in January 2004 on Fell Street in Hayes Valley.
The venue occupies a former TV studio with a mezzanine.
Address: 155 Fell Street, San Francisco

name: Russian Hill Bookstore
summary: Bookstore on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Established in 1974 as a used and new bookstore.
Independently owned by Ben Bellouin and Jess Tsang.
Address: 2162 Polk Street, San Francisco

name: SF Eagle
summary: Bar on 12th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Bob Damron and Jay Levine opened the bar on April 8, 1981.
Named a San Francisco Landmark in October 2021, the city's first leather bar landmark.
Has the only outdoor patio among SoMa leather bars.
Designated: San Francisco Designated Landmark
Address: 398 12th Street, San Francisco

name: Tempest
summary: Pub on Natoma Street, San Francisco.
facts: Has operated since 1986 in Natoma Alley off 5th Street.
The bar has a rustic brick interior and shares a kitchen with Box Kitchen.
Address: 431 Natoma Street, San Francisco

name: Terminus
summary: Small bar with daytime food. Mostly bar seating with a few small tables.
facts: European-style cafe and bar modeled after a train station.
Stands at the end of the California Street cable car line.
Address: 16 California Street, San Francisco

name: The Alembic
summary: Bar on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: Christin Evans and Mikha Diaz acquired the bar in 2018.
Serves spirits, craft beers, local wines and plates.
Has outdoor seating
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 1725 Haight Street, San Francisco

name: The Booksmith
summary: Bookstore on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in October 1976 at 1746 Haight Street.
Moved to 1727 Haight in 2021, the former site of its sister store the Bindery.
Christin Evans and Praveen Madan bought it from founder Gary Frank in 2007.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 1727 Haight Street, San Francisco

name: The Cinch Saloon
summary: Bar on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sold in 2025 to Scott Taylor, beverage director at nearby Harris' Restaurant.
Robby Morgenstein and Bob Thornton owned the bar from 1998.
Address: 1723 Polk Street, San Francisco

name: The Halfway Club
summary: Bar on Geneva Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: A Midwestern-inspired bar that pours a Wisconsin Old-Fashioned with Argonaut Brandy.
Hosts weekly trivia nights, jazz performances and patio concerts.
Has Wi-Fi
Address: 1166 Geneva Avenue, San Francisco

name: The Plough and the Stars
summary: Pub on Clement Street, San Francisco.
facts: The pub opened April 30, 1975 as an Irish pub and live music venue.
The building was constructed in 1905 and housed a French laundry for most of its history.
Address: 116 Clement Street, San Francisco

name: The Regency Ballroom
summary: Nightclub on Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Built in 1909 as a Scottish Rite Masonic temple designed by Albert Roller.
Reopened as the Regency Center in 2002 after decades as a movie theater.
Address: 1300 Van Ness Avenue, San Francisco

name: The Riptide
summary: Bar on Taraval Street, San Francisco.
facts: The building dates to 1941, when it opened as a seaside tavern.
Hosts live music, DJs and karaoke and has a fireplace.
Address: 3639 Taraval Street, San Francisco

name: The Saloon
summary: Bar on Grant Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: First opened in 1861 and originally owned by Ferdinand E. Wagner.
Began as Wagner's Beer Hall and was later renamed the Saloon.
Hosts live music
Address: 1232 Grant Avenue, San Francisco

name: The Stud
summary: Bar on Folsom Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1966 by George Matson and a business partner.
Stud collective members bought the bar and revived it as a co-op in 2017.
Reopened on April 20, 2024, at 1123 Folsom St after closing in 2020.
Address: 1123 Folsom Street, San Francisco

name: Third Rail
summary: Bar on 20th Street, San Francisco.
facts: Serves only cocktails and jerky.
The Red Eye cocktail is spiked with coffee and chili.
Has outdoor seating
Address: 628 20th Street, San Francisco

name: Thrillhouse Records
summary: Record store on Mission Street, San Francisco.
facts: A volunteer-run, not-for-profit punk record store.
Also hosts small punk shows.
Address: 3422 Mission Street, San Francisco

name: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
summary: Bar on Mason Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1945 in the Fairmont's former Terrace Plunge swimming pool.
Has a bandstand on a floating barge and artificial thunderstorms.
Founded in 1945
Address: 950 Mason Street, San Francisco

name: Tony Nik's Cafe
summary: Bar on Stockton Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1933 as Tony Nicco's Cafe, among the first North Beach bars licensed after Prohibition.
A mural by Nadine Torrance from the 1949 remodel is still on the back wall.
Address: 1534 Stockton Street, San Francisco

name: Top of the Mark
summary: Bar on California St, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in 1939 when the Mark Hopkins penthouse became a glass-walled cocktail lounge.
In World War II servicemen had a farewell drink here before shipping out.
The northwest corner was nicknamed Weeper's Corner.
Founded in 1939
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 999 California St, San Francisco

name: Trad'r Sam
summary: Bar on Geary Boulevard, San Francisco.
facts: Poured its first mai tai in 1937, the year the Golden Gate Bridge opened.
Reopened in November 2023 after a temporary closure.
Has Wi-Fi
Address: 6150 Geary Boulevard, San Francisco

name: True Laurel
summary: Bar on Alabama Street, San Francisco.
facts: Comes from the team behind Lazy Bear.
Bar director Nicolas Torres builds science-forward cocktails around local flora.
Wheelchair accessible
Address: 753 Alabama Street, San Francisco

name: Tunnel Records
summary: Record store on Taraval Street, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 2017 by Ben Wintroub, who runs the record shop with a beach goods shop run by Andrea de Francisco.
Wintroub is the great nephew of jazz producer Orrin Keepnews.
Address: 3614 Taraval Street, San Francisco

name: Twin Peaks Tavern
summary: Bar on Castro Street, San Francisco.
facts: Designated San Francisco Landmark #264.
First opened in 1935 and became a gay bar with open plate glass windows in 1972.
Address: 401 Castro Street, San Francisco

name: vinyl dreams
summary: Record store on Haight Street, San Francisco.
facts: Owner Mike Battaglia worked about 15 years at Amoeba Music before starting it.
Opened a brick-and-mortar store in June 2013 after starting as online-only in 2011.
Address: 593 Haight Street, San Francisco

name: White Cap
summary: Bar on Taraval Street, San Francisco.
facts: Surf-themed cocktail bar named for the waves, two blocks from the ocean.
Features the bartending of Carlos Yturria.
Has outdoor seating
Address: 3608 Taraval Street, San Francisco

name: Wild Side West
summary: Bar on Cortland Avenue, San Francisco.
facts: Founded in 1962 by Pat Ramseyer and Nancy White, it began in Oakland.
Moved to Bernal Heights in 1977 and bought an 1890s Italianate-style building.
Named after the 1962 film Walk on the Wild Side.
Founded in 1962
Address: 424 Cortland Avenue, San Francisco

name: Woods Outbound
summary: Bar on Judah Street, San Francisco.
facts: Opened in early 2017 as the fifth brewpub run by Jim Woods in San Francisco and Oakland.
Its opening menu centered on empanadas.
Address: 4045 Judah Street, San Francisco

name: Woods Polk Station
summary: Pub on Polk Street, San Francisco.
facts: Sister location to Cerveceria MateVeza, pouring its own WOODS beers.
Serves empanadas from El Porteno alongside eight rotating taps.
Address: 2255 Polk Street, San Francisco

name: Zeitgeist
summary: Pub on Valencia Street, San Francisco.
facts: The bar dates to 1972 as the Rainbow Cattle Company.
Added to San Francisco's Legacy Business Registry on October 3, 2016.
Has a large outdoor beer garden with picnic tables.
Has outdoor seating
No dogs allowed
Address: 199 Valencia Street, San Francisco
